title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, connector commands, licensing options and governance controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes add-time policy checks from runtime enforcement and leaves standalone connection creation as an open question.

claims.claim: A blockable connector can be blocked at Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote:
Select Security in the navigation pane.
In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy.
From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> classifies connectors in a DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>

The policy name (GUID).

Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The classifications General, Confidential and Blocked correspond to Non-business, Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The standalone pa connection create section of the CLI reference does not describe an ACP or DLP policy check.

claims.quote: Searched: "code apps" "CLI" "preview" "connector". Opened reference/cli, create-connection and quickstart-github-copilot; pa commands have no per-command phase labels. The plugin and the separate legacy pac code family are labelled preview.
